div.head: II Cn 8.2
div.ab: And gyf man þonne þæne gerefan teo, þæt he be his leafe þæt fals worhte, ladige hine mid þryfealdre lade; ⁊ gyf seo lad þonne berste, hæbbe þone ylcan dom, þe se þe þæt fals worhte.
⁊ gyf man ðone refan téo, þæt he be his hléafe þæt fals worhte, ladie hine mid ðryfealdre lade; ⁊ gyf seo lád ðonne byrste, habbe ðone ilcan dóm, ðe se ðe þæt fals worhte.
And gif man þonne þone gerefan teo, þæt he be his leafe þæt fals worhte, ladige hine mid þryfealdre lade; ⁊ gif seo lád þone berste, habbe þonne ylcan dom, se ðe þæt fals worhte.
Si prepositus accusetur, quod eius licentia quis falsum fecerit, purget se triplici lada; quodsi purgatio fregerit, idem iudicium habeat quod qui falsum composuit.

Et si uicecomes (id est prępositus ciuitatis aut uillę) calumniatus fuerit, quod (falsator) per eius licentiam fecisset quod fecit, purget se triplici purgatione, sacramenti aut igniti ferri (id est ordel), quod Angli nominant thrifealde lade (purgamine, q. A. uocant þrefeald l., sa. aut i. f., q. A. uocant ordel); et si ceciderit in purgatione, sustineat quod falsus monetarius sustinuit.
Quod si monetarius prepositum accusauerit, quod illius licencia falsum fabricauerit, purget se triplici purgamine; quod si defecerit, idem iudicium sustineat quod ipse qui illud falsum fabricauit.
⁊ gyf man ðone refan téo, þæt he be his hléafe þæt fals worhte, ladie hine mid ðryfealdre lade, ⁊ gyf seo lád ðonne byrste, habbe ðone ilcan dóm ðe se ðe þæt fals worhte.
And gyf man þonne þæne gerefan teo, þæt he be his leafe þæt fals worhte, ladige hine mid þryfealdre lade; and gyf seo lad þonne berste, hæbbe þone ylcan dom þe se þe þæt fals worhte.

Und wenn nun der Vogt verklagt wird, dass mit dessen Erlaubniss jener diese Fälschung gemacht habe, so reinige er sich mit dreifachem Reinigungsbeweise; und wenn diese Reinigung nun misslingt, so erhalte er dasselbe Strafurtheil, wie der, welcher jene Fälschung gemacht hat.

And if the reeve is then accused of the false coin having been made with his permission, let him clear himself with the threefold clearing; and if the clearing then fails, let him receive the same judgment as he who made the false coin.

And if the reeve is accused of having granted his permission to the man who coined false money, he shall clear himself by the triple oath of exculpation, and if it fails, he shall have the same sentence as the man who has coined the false money.

And if the reeve is accused, that it was with his permission that he coined the false money, he is to clear himself with the three-fold process of exculpation; and if this exculpation fails, he is to incur the same sentence as he who coined the false money.

And if a reeve is charged with permitting the counterfeit to be made, he shall exonerate himself with the threefold oath of exculpation; and if the oath fails, he shall suffer the same penalty as the counterfeiter.

div.note: B's ‘refan’ for ‘gerefan’. Liebermann compares IV Atr 7.3.; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 315, October 2026 (MS Cons)
threefold oath of exculpation: That is, a sworn declaration of innocence supported by the oaths of thirty-six witnesses, as a single oath of exculpation required the support of twelve witnesses.

Für den Ankläger halten Cons Schmid den Münzer [etwa indem er den Auftraggeber zur Gewähr zog?]. Allein man ist allgemeiner, und auch die Quelle verrät nichts von jenem engen Sinne
Cons, Schmid take the moneyer to be the accuser [perhaps by vouching to warranty the man who commissioned him?]. But man is more general, and the source, too, betrays nothing of that narrow sense
‘Sheriff’ Inst i, Schmid zu eng. Richtig bei Inst ii auch Port- und Tungerefa, aber auch das zu eng
‘Sheriff’ Inst i, Schmid: too narrow. Inst ii rightly includes port- and tungerefa as well, but that too is too narrow
Neben Eid setzt alternativ das für ihn einzige Ordal des Glüheisens Inst; vgl. IV Atr 7, 3.—Zur Hk-Glosse der Cons. s. Gl Auswahleid 15, das Dreifache von ebd. 10; Eideshelfer 27c

Alongside the oath, Inst sets as an alternative the ordeal of hot iron, the only one for him; cf. IV Atr 7, 3.—On the Hk gloss in Cons. see Gl Auswahleid 15, three times that of ibid. 10; Eideshelfer 27c
A's þonne ist Acc. von se; s. Wb 192 letzte Z.
A's þonne is the acc. of se; see Wb 192 last l.

It is noteworthy that, about this time, a great deal of false money was produced, not in England but in Scandinavia. Canute’s money is of a very much lighter standard than that of previous kings, but is not bad, see Chadwick, A.S. Institutions, p. 33.

Inst. reads: purget se triplici purgatione, sacramenti aut igniti ferri, cf. IV Atr. 7, 3; Cons. reads: p. s. t. purgamine, one MS adding, cum xliibus legalibus hominibus nominatis, et iuret se tricesima et sexta manu, cf. Leis Wl. 15, 1. The expression probably does refer to an oath of 36 compurgators, cf. the Anglo-Scand. phrase mid þrinna xii in III Atr. 13, which suggests that the normal mode of exculpation was by the oath of 12 compurgators.

note.seg: Here follow VI Ethelred, 32.2 (=III Edgar, 8.1), 32.3 (=V Ethelred, 26.1), concerned with weights and measures and the duties of the repair of boroughs and bridges, and military service. Then come the last two clauses of VI Ethelred (40, 40.1) the second of which =V Ethelred, 33.1. The Nero and Corpus versions of Cnut's laws retain the “Amen” which was in place at the end of VI Ethelred.
